tagline: Connecting people. For a better future.
hero_kpi_rationale: Service revenue is the central pillar of Deutsche Telekom's sustainable growth strategy, capturing value from fixed and mobile networks, as well as emerging digital services such as fiber and IoT. It is the primary driver of FCF trajectory and adjusted operating margin.

kpis.name: Service Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenues from telecom services (mobile, fixed, internet, TV) excluding terminal sales.
kpis.description: Service revenue grew 3.9% in 2024, driven by fiber, 5G, and rising ARPU in the US via T-Mobile.
kpis.signal: Solid growth despite European market maturity.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA AL
kpis.explanation: Gross operating result after rent, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA AL is advancing thanks to T-Mobile US synergies and fixed cost reduction in Europe.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow AL
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after investments, but before dividends and spectrum.
kpis.description: FCF AL surges to €19.2 billion in 2024, supported by EBITDA growth and controlled capex.
kpis.signal: Strong FCF acceleration, sign of capex discipline.

kpis.name: Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue including services and terminal equipment.
kpis.description: Net revenue reaches €115.8 billion in 2024, driven by T-Mobile US and fiber in Europe.
kpis.signal: Stable growth in a mature sector.

kpis.name: Capex (before spectrum)
kpis.explanation: Network infrastructure spending (fiber, 5G, data centers) before spectrum investments.
kpis.description: Capex before spectrum stands at €16.0 billion, slightly declining, focused on fiber and 5G.
kpis.signal: Capex stabilized after reduction, prioritizing profitability.

kpis.name: Return on Capital Employed
kpis.explanation: Profitability generated by capital invested in the company.
kpis.description: ROCE declined to 8.5% in 2024, impacted by fiber and 5G spending, but expected to recover.
kpis.signal: Slight decline despite growth, tied to recent investment.

kpis.name: Employees
kpis.explanation: Number of full-time equivalent employees at reporting date, excluding apprentices.
kpis.description: Headcount slightly declined to 198,000 employees, in line with digital transformation.
kpis.signal: Slight decline, sign of ongoing rationalization.

kpis.name: Mobile Customers
kpis.explanation: Total number of mobile customers worldwide (T-Mobile US included).
kpis.description: Mobile customers reached 261.4 million in 2024, driven by T-Mobile US (+7.2M).
kpis.signal: Sustained growth in the US and Europe.

kpis.name: Broadband and Fiber Customers
kpis.explanation: Number of broadband customers (fiber, cable, DSL) in the group, excluding wholesale.
kpis.description: Broadband customers reached 22.4 million, supported by fiber rollout.
kpis.signal: Steady fiber growth in Germany and Europe.

risks.title: Management instability and operational continuity risk
risks.score_rationale: Multiple Board of Management changes in 2024-2025 (Höttges reassigned, Gopalan dismissed and transferred to T-Mobile US, Diehl appointed). Neutral language but high frequency of transitions. UP trend: 3 major changes in 3 months. Moderate weight: affects strategic continuity in Germany and USA.

risks.title: Strategic dependency on T-Mobile US and governance risks
risks.score_rationale: Four Board of Management members serve on T-Mobile US Board (Höttges Chair, Gopalan, Illek, Langheim). Factual language but notable concentration of power. STABLE trend but structural. High weight: T-Mobile US is major subsidiary (USA is key segment).

risks.title: Regulatory compliance and governance risks in Europe
risks.score_rationale: Dominique Leroy sits on OTE (Greece) and T-Mobile Polska (Poland) boards; presence in 3 countries with distinct telecom regulations. Neutral language but implicit. STABLE trend. Moderate weight: multi-country exposure to heterogeneous regulatory regimes.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and critical sensitive data management
risks.score_rationale: Claudia Nemat (Technology & Innovation) chairs Deutsche Telekom Security GmbH and T-Systems International (T-Systems manages critical IT infrastructure). Implicit language but key role. STABLE trend. High weight: telecom operator equals critical national infrastructure.

risks.title: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in Germany
risks.score_rationale: Srini Gopalan (Germany responsibility until February 2025) and new Rodrigo Diehl assigned to Germany. Neutral language but leadership change on key market. UP trend: transition underway. High weight: Germany equals ~40% of DTE revenue.

risks.title: T-Systems integration and synergy risks
risks.score_rationale: Dr. Ferri Abolhassan appointed T-Systems head since January 2024 (new role). Factual language but T-Systems is strategic segment undergoing transformation. NEW trend: recent appointment. Moderate weight: T-Systems equals B2B IT/services segment in restructuring.

risks.title: Geopolitical exposure and sanctions in European operations
risks.score_rationale: Presence in Poland (T-Mobile Polska) and Greece (OTE); tense geopolitical context (Ukraine, EU-Russia tensions). Language absent from text but implicit. UP trend: rising geopolitical tensions. Moderate weight: operations in sensitive zones.

risks.title: Dependency on critical telecom equipment suppliers
risks.score_rationale: Implicit: telecom operator depends on Nokia, Ericsson, Huawei, ZTE for 5G/network infrastructure. Language absent but structural risk. UP trend: geopolitical tensions affect supply chain. Moderate weight: critical for network rollout.

ai_positioning.summary: Deutsche Telekom is gradually integrating AI into customer services and networks, without making it a central strategic pillar. Focus is on automation and operational efficiency.
evidence: AI use in customer service (chatbots, request routing)
Regional partnerships for AI-based smart city solutions
